class: each case: `plan ROOT --json` read as `plan` (and `plan_wrote`: whether it wrote any file), `apply ROOT --out DIR` read as `applied` (published name -> text); for H11 each tree run on haro: `ran` (the ported) and `ran_ring` (the original)

cases.why: a keyword in another case is lowered; a symbol, a string and a comment are not
asserts:
if 1 = 1 FWrite(stdout, "If") end   # If stays in a comment
x = :Next
for i = 1 to 2 end

cases.why: a built-in is spelled as Haro writes it; a function the tree defines is left as written
Softanza's c is t and its v is x, the same in every file
a bare name in a function is lettered by what it holds; the top level and a class body are not
asserts: 'nCount = 3' in applied['main.haro'] and 'tName = "a"' in applied['main.haro'] and 'aItems = [1, 2]' in applied['main.haro']
'oO = new P' in applied['main.haro'] and '? nCount + 1' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: a method's bare assignment to an attribute of its class is not made a local: refused, named
asserts: any(r['old'] == 'count' and 'attribute' in r['why'] for r in plan['refused'])

cases.why: a rename landing on a name already in the scope is refused, named
asserts: any(r['old'] == 'cName' and r['new'] == 'tName' and 'already' in r['why'] for r in plan['refused'])

cases.why: Softanza's method-local _name_ is unwrapped and lettered as any local
asserts: '? nCount + 1' in applied['main.haro'] and '? tNew' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: an unwrapped name that stands bare and is a keyword in any case is refused, named (the _new_ -> new kind)
asserts: sorted(r['old'] for r in plan['refused'] if 'keyword' in r['why'])

cases.why: a c name whose t name is a keyword-free word is renamed: tAnd is no keyword
plan writes nothing; apply writes every .ring as .haro, and rewrites its loads
a lettered local landing on a name already in its function is refused, named
asserts: any(r['old'] == 'count' and r['new'] == 'nCount' and 'already' in r['why'] for r in plan['refused'])

cases.why: an attribute written with its @ in a method is no refusal; Softanza's c is t there too
asserts: any(r['old'] in ('@cLast', '@tLast') for r in plan['refused'])

cases.why: a load on a first line after a byte order mark is rewritten, the mark kept
a $_name global is $name in every file
a $_name landing on a $name already in the tree is refused, named
asserts: any(r['old'] == '$_tTotal' and 'already' in r['why'] for r in plan['refused'])

cases.why: a call to a function the tree declares is written as it is declared
asserts: '? Shout("a")' in applied['main.haro'] and '? Shout("b")' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: a name the tree declares in two spellings is refused, named
asserts: any(r['old'] == 'mix' and 'two spellings' in r['why'] for r in plan['refused'])

cases.why: :key = value is the pair [:key, value], the value read to its depth's comma or bracket
with --unit, a function in a file the unit never loads leaves the built-in respelled
a pair's value goes on past a line that ends in an operator, as Ring reads it
an unwrapped _cName_ takes Softanza's c rule too: tName
asserts: 'tPath = "a"' in applied['main.haro'] and '? tPath' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: (a) a parameter keeps its p mark: pc is pt, pa with an element letter is pv with it, pn and pb stay
asserts: func f(ptName, pnAt, pbOk, pviPos, paList)
'? ptName + pnAt' in applied['main.haro'] and '? Len(pviPos) + Len(paList)' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: (b) a b name given 1 or 0 is given true or false; a condition on a 1 or 0 literal is true or false
asserts: '\twhile true' in applied['main.haro'] and '\tif false' in applied['main.haro'] and '\t@bOpen = false' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: (c) Softanza's two-letter list letters are v and the element's letter
asserts: 'viPos = [1]' in applied['main.haro'] and 'vtNames = ["a"]' in applied['main.haro'] and 'voItems = []' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: (d) an ALL_CAPS name takes its letter by what it holds, its capitals kept
asserts: '$tSEP = "-"' in applied['main.haro'] and '$dRATE = 0.5' in applied['main.haro'] and '@tNL = "n"' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: (d) a capitalised attribute takes its letter first: 1 or 0 alone is a boolean, a count is a number
asserts: '@bCaseSensitive = true' in applied['main.haro'] and '@nCount = 0' in applied['main.haro'] and '@tTitle = "t"' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: every block ends with end, and a definition's end word goes, leaving its line
asserts: [w for w in ('ok', 'off', 'done', 'other', '{', '}') if w in applied['main.haro']]
'\tcase 1 FWrite(stdout, "b")' in applied['main.haro'] and '\telse FWrite(stdout, "c")' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: one word each, from, #, this outside a brace, parameters in parentheses and none without, no trailing period
asserts: 'class Q from P' in applied['main.haro'] and '? ClassName(this) # the object' in applied['main.haro']
[l for l in applied['main.haro'].splitlines() if l.startswith(('def h(', 'def k'))]
' and not ' in applied['main.haro'] and ' or ' in applied['main.haro'] and '\telseif ' in applied['main.haro']
'\t\tFWrite(stdout, "x")' in applied['main.haro'] and '\t\tgive ' in applied['main.haro'] and '\th(1, 0)\n' in applied['main.haro']

cases.why: a tree in every spelling ported runs on haro and prints what it printed

every definition ends with end; a definition after a class is its method, def; private ends the method before it; a one-line definition's body goes to its own line; the lines after a blank line keep their numbers
a dot that ends a line continues a chain: it moves to the start of the next line; a call's period before a keyword goes
a definition whose name starts with a digit loses its empty parentheses
asserts: [l for l in applied['main.haro'].splitlines() if 'Hearts' in l or 'Ways' in l]

cases.why: see and put: a line that ends with + nl prints with print, any other writes through the stream
null is written "", and isnull is IsEmpty
the ported tree runs on haro and prints what the classic Ring surface printed
